newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IMF sees accord on capital increase in September.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees accord on capital increase in September.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual meeting to take place in September was expected to reach a decision on an increase in the organisation's capital base, a senior IMF information officer said on Monday.
"We are expecting a number of significant decisions to be taken by our ministers in Hong Kong in September," Deputy Chief Information Officer Graham Newman told reporters.

The top item on the agenda was an increase in the capital base of the IMF, Newman said. The capital currently totals around US$220 billion, and there were various proposals on the table to increase that by 50 to 100 percent, he said.
A decision on the allocation of Special Drawing Rights to members that have joined the IMF since 1982 and have never received their allocations, was also expected.
An agreement on changing the IMF's statutes to give the organisation a mandate to oversee capital movements was also expected, Newman said.

The IMF currently only has jurisdiction over the current account, but given the globalisation of the world economy the membership felt it needed jurisdiction over the capital account as well, he explained.
European monetary union and the move toward a single currency was also likely to be a major topic at the September meeting in Hong Kong, he added.
